label: CISA lists it
closed_by: story-site, seeded on 27 October from the newsroom's records (state.json v0 to v3, sources.json by published date, the timeline, the compromise and impact ledgers, BREAKING-001); from Day 7 on, the desk

headline._: Late in the day, CISA adds both flaws to its list of vulnerabilities known to be exploited. No victim is named.
headline.exec: CISA now says both flaws are exploited. No organisation says it was hit. US agencies must patch by 29 October; so should you.
headline.general: The US government now says criminals are using these flaws. If someone runs your website, ask them if it is updated.
headline.security: KEV: both CVEs added 26 October, due 29 October, ransomware use "Unknown". Treat as exploited; hunt as well as patch.
headline.engineer: Nothing new to install. Exploited is now official: confirm the fixed version is what is running, after the restart.
headline.journalist: "Exploited" is now CISA's word, from 26 October. "Hacked" is not: no named victim. Keep the two apart.
headline.researcher: KEV catalogue 2026.10.26 lists both; the evidence behind the listing is not public.

items.text: Extended support vendors ship the fix for out-of-support PHP 5.3 to 8.1.
CPO Magazine: a threat actor targeted PHP flaws days before the disclosure.
A newspaper reports attempts in the millions but no successful code execution in the investigations it cites.
CISA adds both CVEs to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue: added 26 October, due 29 October, ransomware use unknown.
